description.value: The study investigated whether happy, angry, and neutral facial expression primes modulate neural and subjective responses to subsequent negative and neutral pictures during an fMRI emotion-rating task.

spans.text: In the current study, we investigated the effect of happy and angry facial expression primes on subsequent emotional responses to negative stimuli.

value: We predicted that happy facial primes would reduce activity in the amygdala and emotional arousal in response to the subsequently presented negative pictures relative to neutral pictures, as compared with angry facial primes.
Furthermore, we also predicted that happy facial primes would elicit activity in the areas of the prefrontal cortex (PFC) implicated in emotion regulation.
